chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
About a man in janabah: would it suffice him for ghusl al-janabah to stand in the rain until his head and body are washed, while he has access to water other than that?
So he said: If it washes him in the manner of his washing with water, that suffices for him.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him; it fulfilled the legal requirement
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَطَرِ: rainwater used here as the means of washing
key_terms.جَسَدُهُ: his body, indicating the full bodily washing required
key_terms.رَأْسُهُ: his head, mentioned as part of the body to be washed
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water, the standard medium of ritual washing

ai.seo_question: Can a person perform ghusl al-janabah by standing in the rain?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning ghusl al-janabah and whether rainfall can suffice in place of ordinary water usage. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that if the rain washes the person in a manner equivalent to washing with water, then it is sufficient.
